name: latex-render
description: Renders LaTeX in Claude's replies, live and in place: display and inline math and TikZ figures as crisp images (kitty graphics protocol)

images.title: Display math as images
images.description: auto: on in kitty, Ghostty and WezTerm outside tmux; on: always; off: Unicode text only

color.title: Formula color
color.description: Hex color such as #e6e6e6, or auto to follow the light or dark theme

scale.title: Formula scale
scale.description: Terminal rows taken by one line of LaTeX text (1.25 is a little larger than the text around it)

cellAspect.title: Cell aspect ratio
cellAspect.description: Height of a terminal cell divided by its width; raise it if formulas look squashed, lower it if they look stretched

preamble.title: Extra LaTeX preamble
preamble.description: Added after amsmath, amssymb, mathtools and bm, e.g. \usepackage{physics}

background.title: Figure background
background.description: Hex color of the terminal's background on a dark theme, which TikZ's white and color tints such as blue!20 are drawn against; auto is #1e1e1e

preview.title: Live preview
preview.description: on: while Claude writes, text from the first math on is held back and drawn typeset right under the reply, so raw LaTeX never shows; off: the reply streams raw and is typeset when its block ends

inlineImages.title: Inline math as images
inlineImages.description: on: inline $…$ is typeset by LaTeX and drawn inside the line (a line with a tall formula grows to two rows); off: inline math as Unicode text

inlineScale.title: Inline formula scale
inlineScale.description: Size of inline formulas relative to the terminal text; raise it if they look small

inlineBaseline.title: Inline baseline
inlineBaseline.description: Where the terminal font's baseline sits in a cell, as a fraction of its height from the top; nudge it if inline formulas sit too high or too low

displayAlign.title: Display math alignment
displayAlign.description: left: display formulas and figures at the left margin; center: centred across the reply's width
